subject: Post-call: MAP milestones — legal redlines & owner commitments
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@finexa.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@finexa.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: MAP milestones — legal redlines & owner commitments

Hi Laura / team,

Great conversation today — appreciate the clarity on Finexa's deployment timeline and the questions on data residency and the SLA. Attached is the MAP v0.2 (spreadsheet) capturing the milestones we discussed. Please consider this a working draft. Key items I want to highlight so we can lock responsibility and timelines: 

- Target signature date: 2027-03-03 (three-week cadence to allow procurement + legal review).
- MAP milestone: Legal redlines (MSA / DPA / SLA)
  - Owner (Finexa): please provide your redlines back in a single consolidated redline file by EOD 2027-02-17 if possible.
  - Owner (Redwood): Aditya Rao (cc'd) will be the primary reviewer and will handle Redwood's edits/response.
  - Turnaround expectation: Redwood proposes to respond to submitted redlines within 3 business days for routine/clarifying edits. For substantive scope/SLA changes we will need up to 5 business days.
- Dependencies: SOC 2 evidence (we can share current report), final pricing approval from Finexa procurement, and confirmation of data region.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Laura/procurement: confirm who will consolidate redlines (name + email) and whether Feb 17 works as the redline cutoff.
2) Finexa: flag any SLA items you expect to be non-standard so we can triage early.
3) Marissa (AE): I'll coordinate procurement timelines and track the MAP milestones; please expect to be copied on decision threads.

Attachments: 2027-02-10_MAP_v0.2.xlsx (MAP draft) — row-wise milestones + owners. Finexa_Risk_QA.pdf (requested risk questions we discussed).

If you prefer tighter SLAs on turnaround, call that out and we can see what can be expedited.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Laura Chen <laura@finexa.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@finexa.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: MAP milestones — legal redlines & owner commitments

Thanks, Naomi — useful summary. Two quick notes from our side: 

1) Procurement prefers to consolidate a single redline doc. I (Laura) will take point unless procurement pushes back; they are looped.
2) On turnaround: Feb 17 redline cutoff is fine. On Redwood's turnaround, can you confirm if a 2-business-day response is possible for most edits? Our program timeline is tight and a shorter cycle removes friction for our internal stakeholders.

I will scan the MAP and flag any SLA expectations that are likely to be non-standard by tomorrow.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform Partnerships, Finexa Health
laura@finexa.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura@finexa.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: MAP milestones — legal redlines & owner commitments

Laura — thanks for the quick reply and for offering to consolidate. Proposal to reconcile expectations so we can lock the MAP: 

- Finexa provides consolidated redlines by EOD 2027-02-17.
- Redwood commits to the following: 
  - 2 business days turnaround for clarifying/non-substantive edits (typos, definition clarifications, minor wording adjustments).
  - Up to 5 business days for substantive redlines that affect scope, SLA thresholds, or data residency clauses.
- Primary points of contact: Aditya Rao (legal) will handle Redwood responses; Marissa Cole will handle procurement coordination.

If this works, I'll update MAP v0.2 to include explicit owners and the turnaround windows, and send v0.3 by EOD. Marissa, can you confirm procurement timelines on your end so we can update the MAP target close if needed?

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura@finexa.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: MAP milestones — legal redlines & owner commitments

Hi all — looping in with legal's process and SLAs for clarity. Confirming the commitments Naomi laid out and adding a few operational notes: 

- Submission format: please send a single consolidated redline (Word or PDF with track changes/comments) to make review deterministic.
- Turnaround matrix (Redwood legal):
  - Non-substantive edits (definitions, wording, punctuation): 2 business days turnaround from receipt.
  - Substantive redlines (changes to indemnity, liability caps, SLA uptime %, data residency or retention changes): 5 business days.
  - If an SLA or DPA request requires product-side engineering changes (e.g., new region or custom retention), we will surface the dependency in our response and the MAP will reflect an additional dependency item.
- Escalations: for exceptions that require C-level approval (non-standard liability or extended SLA credits), allow an additional 3 business days for internal review/approval.

I'll review Finexa's consolidated file as soon as it's available. If you want an even tighter 2-day SLA for all redlines, we can try to expedite but will ask for a clear definition of "non-substantive" items upfront to reduce churn.

Attaching Finexa_Risk_QA.pdf in case it helps pre-empt common questions.

-Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
note: Thread preserves realistic quoting and attachments; MAP spreadsheet referenced as 2027-02-10_MAP_v0.2.xlsx
